1. If the opponent is dewarding you never place a new observer where they dewarded, even if you kill off their sentry, they will likely place another one in the same spot as before, so ward nearby, but out of range of where their sentry was, so that you don't lose your observer, and they lose gold.

  2. If the enemy has a jungler they will likely only have one support, consider picking an invis hero such as riki/bh/nyx. Bounty hunter especially is good at disrupting an opponents jungle even in the early levels, and they'll only have the one support that will want to buy detection. This will push a 5-role support into the 6-role, and if played right ruin their jungler and mid too. (axe is especially nice to screw over as you can deny his tranquil boots, so keep an eye out for that little box)

  3. There is a rock-paper-scissors like relationship in dota of gank-push-farm. If the enemy is ganking you heavily, group up and take objectives, you can't gank into a group as easily. If they are grouping to take objectives use 2-3 heroes to delay them as much as possible (creep cutting, wave clearing etc) and then farm the rest of the map with the remaining heroes, if they persist you will gain more gold and exp from the trade. If they are farming, they are split up, so gank them, and punish them for spreading out.

  4. Everyone can buy wards, everyone can buy dust. If the enemy has an invis hero there is no point going to gank them without dust, if you have a slot, fill it with dust, if you want to farm one lane for a while, place some sentries. They will save your life, therefore saving you more gold than they cost, or they will earn a kill, that then also covers their costs. Either way, detection is everyone's job. Another thing to note is invis heroes often have diffusal, if you have 2 people carrying dust, they have a sad sad riki.

  5. If you're moaning that your allies didn't follow you in it's almost certainly your fault. However well it would have gone, you probably just overextended and your allies didn't want to take the risk, and so abandoned you to your fate instead of joining you in it. Look back at your play rather than immediately judging them.

  6. Mid isn't there to gank, never ask this, in fact, why not gank mid yourself if you're a support, this should be does as often as possible so long as your carry can farm effectively in lane while you are gone (you might want to consider pulling the creeps into the easy camp then smoking and going straight to mid, it makes the enemy laner less suspicious and less likely to call missing, as the lane was pulled).

  7. Respect the day/night phase, if you want to gank, night time gives a lot of advantages, same with warding, the enemy wards will see just as far, but you're less likely to be spotted by an enemy hero. If it's daytime you shouldn't gank as much and should farm more, as the bonus vision helps protect you from ganks. Also if you're one of the heroes that has high night vision, and the enemy team don't have any, this is abusable, when pushing (even lategame) push when it's night time and your team should have the advantage.

  8. This one is my bitchy one. If you are a support (4-5 role) that can afford to die harass the enemy players in the all chat, call them out on their mistakes, make a big thing about killing them. Just killed the enemy mid twice with smoke ganks? 'Look at your noob mid, dying twice to the same trick'. This invokes rage towards you, and makes the enemy feel far more satisfied killing you than killing your teammates, you know, the carry and such, that they should be killing. I've had a lion and lina ult used on me as a venomancer, after using all my spells, and then have the enemy team gloat about my death as we took throne from the 5/1 teamfight.

  9. Use the all chat to bait an enemy. Just saying stuff like 'rosh' in the all chat can make people want to go and check it, if you're lying in wait it can be easy kills. Even things like baiting out an AA ult to the rosh pit before you storm highground can be game winning. Also say 'press j' it's the default hotkey for fortify, if they fall for it they waste it, and that can win you a game.

  10. If the enemy team harass you in any way mute them immediately. Don't fight back, don't retaliate, just mute them. I would do this to teammates too but they can come in handy every now and again. You can also mute all the enemies from the start if you like.

  11. "We judge others based on their actions, we judge ourselves based on our intentions." This is incredibly important to consider when playing dota, when you screw up you might thing 'but if it had worked...' etc, whereas you don't give that chance to your allies.

Cool list. I just started getting into Dota 2. My biggest question is how are the roles played in the game. For example in league of legends there is one ranged sustained damage carry(bot lane), one burst magic/physical carry(mid lane), one support(bot lane), one jungler, and one tank/brawler(top lane). What are the combinations that are in Dota2?

Ok so first of all let me explain the lanes.

In LoL you have the bot/mid/top on both sides and they generally serve the same purpose. In Dota you can still refer to the lanes by top, mid and bot, but the lanes are lebelled as 'safe lane', 'offlane' and mid. Your team's safelane meets the enemy team's offlane and visa versa. For radiant their safelane is bot and their offlane is top, the is the opposite on dire.

Thye safe lane is the lane next to your allied jungle, which lets you pull the creeps and gives you a lot more safety. The offlane gives less protection to being ganked and the enemy has the ability to pull the lane, which reduces your farm and exp.

Generally the meta in dota is a trilane on the safelane, a solo hero on hte offlane, and a solo mid (1/1/3). You can however run dual lanes (2/1/2) or have a jungler or roaming support (1/1/2 + jungler/roamer). Overall the meta is far more flexible in dota than in LoL.

Instead of having hard carry, top, mid, support, jungler, etc. In dota the roles are mainly given by farming priority, 1-5.

Farming priority 1 is the safelane carry, they will often be heroes that need a lot of gold to be effective, they may have a weak early game presence because of this, and therefore need supports in lane to keep them alive.

Farming priority 2 is usually the mid, they should get lots of exp and gold though not as much as the safelaner, these heroes are generally nukers that can dominate mid lane.

Farming priority 3 is usually the offlane solo hero and is often someone that can manage with nothing but exp, some offlaners also have some potential for getting kills (even 1 vs 3) or disrupting the farm of the enemy carry. Their job more than anything is to not die, and make the enemy carry get as little farm as possible.

Farming priority 4 is the 'farming' support, this doesn't mean they'll actually farm a lane, but this will be for heroes like earthshaker who needs a blink (2250 gold). This role can also be for a jungler, or a roamer, which then leaves you with a solo support in the 5 role.

Farming priority 5 is the 'ward bitch'. This is a support that is expected to buy all the wards, this is usually a hero that can function well with very little farm or exp, such as shadow demon, jakiro etc.

Even these are subject to change, you can have your 3 role playing solo safe lane, as a hero that would usually be played offlane, then have a trilane on the offlane. This is very strong if the 3 heroes you choose have very good kill potential. You can have 2 roaming supports and 3 solo lanes, or a roamer + a jungler and 3 solo lanes. In which case your 1 role has to be a hero that can survive alone and dominate their lane very easily.

There's also no fixed role for most heroes, while some are pretty secure (eg spectre is a carry for 1 role) some of them are quite flexible, wraith king for instance can be played as a 1 role, a 4 role in the jungle, or a support in the 4 or 5 role. Venomancer is generally a 4 or 5 role support, but you can also play him offlane or mid. There are lots of things you can try in dota that you would get reported for in LoL.

If you have any more questions or want me to explain anything further feel free to pm me or reply to this.

I'm new to the site and was looking into how this site's voting structure was set up when I came across this line:

Votes are associated with your IP address. That means you cannot vote on the same post or comment using alternate accounts. Only the first vote will be counted.

Doesn't that cause a problem in a lot of households? My house, for instance, has three occupants and we all have the same public IP. Question about Voat's restriction of daily upvoats by IP address

Sure, if multiple devices share the same IP, then they wouldn't be able to vote on the same comments and submissions twice. It hasn't really been a problem here and it really isn't Voat's problem if devices share the same IPs. The measure prevents issues with single IPs mass voting with different accounts.

Perhaps a better method'll come along, but this is what we have.

Home routers NAT, so most households have multiple people on the same public IP. It hasn't been a problem yet, but it will be if the site continues to grow. I believe some colleges NAT as well, which makes it significantly worse.

I understand your point outside of this line

it really isn't Voat's problem if devices share the same IPs

I disagree with you on that point as this is an artificial limit that might actually hinder Voat in expanding beyond where it currently is. Now, if that's the goal or the intention, disregard entirely. I'm just looking at this from the viewpoint of, "Reddit is on fire, everyone jump in the Voat Boat", and how much of an opportunity they have currently to capitalize on this window.

In the end I'm sure the whole platform will be tweaked, especially considering it's just in Alpha. I just wanted to put the question out there as I've never seen IP addresses as an effective way to meter or monitor anything on the internet, mainly for the NAT and shared public IP reasons you've seen discussed in this thread already.
I'm on a VPN and rarely even know what country my IP is in. Is that going to present a problem for me? An opportunity for evil?

A little from column A, a little from column B.

If you wanted to 'cheat' the system, you could disconnect and reconnect your VPN after voting, and then you'd probably be on a different IP address and be able to vote again from a different account. (I'm not advocating for this, of course, but I don't believe there's any value in security through obfuscation.)

The flip side is that your VPN has a finite number of public-facing IP addresses and there's always a nonzero chance that someone else has voted on the same post as you while using the same VPN with same IP address... but that sounds unlikely to be a frequent problem.

It's not just households that this affects. My entire company of a thousand people are NAT'd so this could become a significant issue as voat becomes more popular.

It would be nice if they could implement a timestamp and made it so the same IP can't vote twice within 15 minutes or such (exact cooldown TBD). It would still throttle mass voting attacks but allow people that share an IP some more flexibility.

The easiest way to get around the command line is just googling the sorts of things you need to do and trying to understand what the command is actually doing.
